newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Largest Yugo brokerage turnover sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Largest Yugo brokerage turnover sharply up.

text.p: The largest Yugoslav brokerage house, Trziste Novca, reported on Thursday a healthy 38 percent rise in 1996 turnover.
Trziste Novca's January-October turnover rose to 2.312 billion dinars ($464 million), up 38 percent on the whole of 1995.
This compares to 1.9 billion dinars traded from January to October 1996 on the official Belgrade bourse.

Nikola Arandjelovic, head of Trziste Novca, said short-term securities accounted for 37 percent of the 10-month turnover while the remaining 63 percent were generated from so-called giro money transactions.
Only banks are allowed to participate in the unofficial giro money market, trading surplus liquidity.

"The share of short-term securities in our total turnover was particularly high over 1994 and 1995. But in May 1996 it began to shrink due to some changes in central bank policy," Arandjelovic told reporters.
He said any increase in securities trade could only come after the state appears on the market with its own securities.

"It is therefore encouraging that the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) plans to convert part of the public debt and some banks' and companies' liabilities to securities and sell them on the financial market," Arandjelovic said.
Such a move confirms that the NBY is committed to developing the Yugoslav financial market, he added.

According to a report presented by Trziste Novca, its October turnover stood at 298 million dinars, with 213 million generated from the giro money deals while short-term securities accounted for the remaining 86 million dinars.
Trziste Novca, first established in November 1989 as the official money market of the former Yugoslavia, conducted its first transactions on November 14.
